item.title: PLA conducts combat readiness patrols around China's Huangyan Dao
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-31
PLA conducts combat readiness patrols around China's Huangyan Dao BEIJING, Oct. 30 (Xinhua) -- Naval and air units of the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Southern Theater Command (STC) on Friday conducted combat readiness patrols in the territorial sea and airspace of China's Huangyan Dao and its surrounding areas. "This is a necessary countermeasure in response to the Philippines' rights-violation and provocative acts," the theater command said in a statement. Noting that Huangyan Dao is China's inherent territory, the STC said since the start of October, its forces have strengthened readiness patrols in the territorial sea and airspace of Huangyan Dao and its surrounding areas. The patrols are aimed at further enhancing control and management over relevant waters and airspace, and serve as an effective countermeasure to cope with all sorts of rights-violation and provocative acts, according to the statement. "Forces of the STC will resolutely safeguard China's sovereignty and security and firmly uphold peace and stability in the South China Sea," it said. Also on Friday, the China Coast Guard conducted law-enforcement patrols near Huangyan Dao, which it also said was a necessary countermeasure in response to the Philippines' rights-violation and provocative acts. item.title: China's manufacturing PMI softens, high-tech sector maintains expansion
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-31
China's manufacturing PMI softens, high-tech sector maintains expansion BEIJING, Oct. 31 (Xinhua) -- China's manufacturing activity moderated in October, with the purchasing managers' index (PMI) falling to 49.3, while high-tech and equipment manufacturing sectors maintained expansion, official data showed Saturday. The overall reading was down 0.8 percentage points from the previous month, according to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS). Huo Lihui, a chief statistician with the NBS, attributed the retreat to some demand being brought forward ahead of the National Day holiday earlier this month and a complex international environment. The production sub-index stood at 49.8, down 1.9 points from September, while the new orders sub-index fell 1.1 points to 49.4, as both supply and demand moderated during the month. The PMI for high-tech manufacturing stood at 51.3, while that for equipment manufacturing came in at 50.6, both remaining above the 50-point threshold that separates expansion from contraction. The figures indicate that emerging industries continued to sustain growth momentum, supported by the ongoing development of new quality productive forces, Huo noted. Manufacturing activity in several advanced industries remained robust. Both the production and new orders sub-indexes for railway, shipbuilding and aerospace equipment manufacturing, as well as computer, communications and electronic equipment manufacturing, stood at 53 or above, pointing to relatively strong supply and demand in these sectors. Large manufacturers continued to report expansion, with their PMI standing at 50.2, despite a slight decline of 0.4 points from the previous month. Meanwhile, the PMI readings for medium-sized and small enterprises came in at 48.4 and 47.5, respectively. On the price front, both major raw material purchasing prices and factory-gate prices remained in expansionary territory, although their growth moderated. The purchasing price sub-index stood at 56.8, down 4 points from September, while the factory-gate price sub-index eased 2.3 points to 51.7, partly reflecting recent declines in the prices of certain nonferrous metals and other commodities. item.title: China supports South Africa's continued participation in activities under G20 framework
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-31
China supports South Africa's continued participation in activities under G20 framework: FM spokesperson BEIJING, Oct. 30 (Xinhua) -- China supports the continued participation of South Africa in relevant activities under the G20 framework, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Friday. Guo made the remarks at a regular press briefing in response to a question about South Africa not being invited to the G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting to be held in Atlanta, the United States. The G20 is the premier forum for international economic cooperation and plays an important role in advancing multilateralism, promoting world economic growth and improving global governance, Guo said. item.title: Preparations for APEC CEO Summit in south China enter final stage: CCPIT
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-31
Preparations for APEC CEO Summit in south China enter final stage: CCPIT BEIJING, Oct. 30 (Xinhua) -- Preparations for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 have entered the last stage, with work progressing in an orderly manner ahead of the Nov. 17-18 event in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade (CCPIT) said on Friday. The summit, hosted by the CCPIT under the theme "To Prosper and Win the Future Together," will bring together political and business representatives from APEC economies. Several leaders of APEC economies will deliver speeches or take part in panel discussions, and have direct exchanges with business leaders from across the region, according to Wang Wenshuai, spokesperson for the CCPIT. Business representatives from all 21 APEC economies have registered to attend the event, with well-known companies from non-APEC economies, including Britain, France, Germany and Switzerland, also signing up, Wang said. The agenda in Shenzhen will cover a range of topics, such as the building of the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific, connectivity, artificial intelligence, the digital economy, the development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, sustainable development, and digital and green transformation. Meanwhile, the APEC Business Advisory Council (ABAC), a mechanism through which the regional business community participates in APEC cooperation and submits policy recommendations to APEC economy leaders, will hold its fourth meeting of the year in Shenzhen from Nov. 14 to 16. Under its annual theme of "Openness, Connectivity and Synergy," this ABAC meeting will focus on regional economic integration, sustainable development, connectivity and digital innovation, and review the year's work and discuss priorities for next year. The council has already held three meetings in 2026, which took place in Jakarta, Mexico City and Bangkok, producing 14 outcome documents. The CEO Summit will draw on ABAC's policy recommendations for the year and discussions held during the summit to jointly issue a Shenzhen initiative with the Asia-Pacific business community, Wang noted. The initiative will align with the theme of APEC China 2026, "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," and reflect the business community's commitment to promoting openness, inclusive development, innovation, connectivity and mutually beneficial cooperation across the region, said Wang. As the host of APEC in 2026, China will hold the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen on Nov. 18 and 19. The APEC CEO Summit will be held on the sidelines of this meeting. This is the third time China has hosted APEC, and the first time in 12 years. During the 2026 APEC "China Year," some 300 events are expected to take place across multiple cities in China, according to the Chinese foreign ministry. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: CPC advances Party self-governance with resolute anti-graft efforts
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-31
CPC advances Party self-governance with resolute anti-graft efforts The Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) holds a press conference on the guiding principles from the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee on Oct. 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhang Xiaoyu) BEIJING, Oct. 30 (Xinhua) -- The Communist Party of China (CPC) remains resolute in its fight against corruption as part of broader efforts to advance full and rigorous Party self-governance, according to Party officials. At a plenum that concluded Thursday, the CPC Central Committee adopted a resolution on persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, stressing the need to maintain a tough stance against corruption and strengthen checks on and oversight over the exercise of power. The Fifth Plenary Session of the 20th CPC Central Committee also called for fortifying the cultural-ethical foundations for championing integrity and disdaining graft, and enhancing coordinated efforts to ensure that officials do not have the audacity, opportunity, or desire to commit corruption. "The anti-graft fight remains a grave and complex challenge, and much remains to be done to eliminate the conditions and fertile ground that give rise to corruption," senior anti-graft official Zhang Fuhai said on Friday at a press conference held by the CPC Central Committee on the guiding principles from the plenum. Since 2012, discipline inspection and supervisory organs across the country have filed 8.105 million cases and punished 7.922 million people, including 963 officials registered with and supervised by the CPC Central Committee, said Zhang, deputy secretary of the CPC Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and deputy head of the National Commission of Supervision. China has over the years launched an unprecedented anti-graft campaign that has reached every level of the Party and government, netting both high-ranking "tigers" and lower-level "flies." Some of the most senior officials -- including former members of the Political Bureau and its Standing Committee, senior military officials, and retirees who left their leading positions years ago -- have been brought to justice. The campaign has continued unabated. In 2025 alone, 115 officials at ministerial level or above were placed under investigation, while 627,000 people were disciplined in cases involving misconduct and graft that affect the people's immediate interests. The same year, China also opened investigations into more than 500 cases of cross-border corruption. It was noted at the plenum this week that the Party must steadfastly follow a distinctive Chinese path of anti-graft and strengthen the Party Central Committee's centralized, unified leadership over anti-corruption work. "We must take systematic steps to address both symptoms and root causes of corruption and adopt a holistic approach that combines severe punishment, targeted remedy, and effective prevention, carrying this fight through to the end," said a communique issued after the plenary session. Zhang said anti-graft authorities will, in line with the arrangements made at the plenum, resolutely win the battle against corruption. "This is a battle that we cannot afford to lose and must never lose." The plenum pledged to take targeted, well-designed measures to select and appoint officials, inspire them to foster and act on the correct view of performance, and enhance their competence in fulfilling duties and breaking new ground. Huang Jianfa, deputy head of the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee, said at the press conference that strict discipline is not intended to stifle initiative or constrain officials' actions. "Rather, it seeks to set clear direction, enforce rules, promote sound conduct and guard against corruption, fostering a clean political environment and enabling officials to take initiative in their work," he said. The resolution stresses that everyone is equal before the rules, no one enjoys privileges and no exceptions are allowed in their enforcement, said Xie Chuntao, vice president of the Party School of the CPC Central Committee. It also calls for enforcement and oversight to be integrated into every stage of the work of Party organizations, members and officials, ensuring that institutional rules remain authoritative at all times and effective at every level, Xie said at the press conference. Discipline inspection and supervision officers communicate with local villagers in Zhongba Village of Luliang County in Qujing City, southwest China's Yunnan Province, Feb. 24, 2026. (Photo by Wang Yong/Xinhua) FULL, RIGOROUS PARTY SELF-GOVERNANCE The plenum made systematic plans for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance. Key priorities include strengthening the Party spirit, improving conduct and tightening discipline, taking firm and coordinated action against corruption, running the Party with systems and regulations, and refining Party and state oversight systems. With over 100 million members, the Party has attached great importance to its own building since it was founded in 1921, said Liu Haixing, a member of the CPC Central Committee and head of the International Department of the CPC Central Committee. For 105 years, he added, Party members have treated Party building as a great project, pressing ahead one generation after another -- forging and tempering the Party into the great, glorious and correct CPC that stands today. "The Party demonstrates the strong vitality of Marxism," he said. As profound changes unseen in a century gather pace across the world, political parties around the globe are confronting a stream of new issues and challenges. "Many political parties are turning their eyes to us in the hope of finding paths and solutions for reference," said Liu. That attention, he noted, attests to the valuable experience the CPC has accumulated during the periods of revolution, development and reform -- experience that progressive forces around the world can draw on. Delivery rider Gao Feng with Meituan, an on-demand delivery platform, speaks during a Party branch meeting in Beijing, capital of China, June 18, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhang Chenlin) Wu Hansheng, head of the Society Work Department of the CPC Central Committee, underscored the importance of Party building in emerging sectors. Wu's department will work to expand the coverage of Party organizations in these sectors, strengthen Party building and improve services and management for people in new forms of employment. Built on internet platforms, new forms of employment now engage some 84 million workers nationwide, including couriers, ride-hailing drivers and e-commerce workers. Zhong Baijun, party chief of Xijidang Village in Lianyungang City in east China's Jiangsu Province, who attended the plenum as a non-voting participant, said that for communities like the one he leads, the latest arrangements from the meeting mean power at the micro level must be kept in check, affairs handled fairly, and petty graft close to the people rooted out. The aim, he said, is to win public trust with integrity and clean governance. "Weeds don't stop growing just because you've pulled them once," said Zhong, adding that the same goes for the Party's full and rigorous self-governance. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: Peng Liyuan chats over tea with wife of German president
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-31
Peng Liyuan chats over tea with wife of German president Peng Liyuan, wife of Chinese President Xi Jinping, chats over tea with Elke Budenbender, wife of German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 30, 2026. Budenbender is accompanying her husband who is on a state visit to China. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) BEIJING, Oct. 30 (Xinhua) -- Peng Liyuan, wife of Chinese President Xi Jinping, chatted over tea with Elke Budenbender, wife of German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, in Beijing on Friday. Budenbender is accompanying her husband who is on a state visit to China until Oct. 31. Peng happily recalled her trip accompanying President Xi on his visit to Germany in 2017 and expressed her appreciation for Budenbender's long-standing commitment to safeguarding the rights and interests of women and children. They watched a short film on the cultural and people-to-people exchanges between China and Germany. Peng noted that the cooperation between China and Germany in areas such as education and culture is rich and diverse. She expressed the hope that the people from both countries will maintain frequent exchanges, continuously enhance mutual understanding, and promote closer bonds between the two peoples. Budenbender expressed heartfelt gratitude for Peng's hospitality and her appreciation for Peng's work on cultural and people-to-people exchanges between Germany and China. She stated her willingness to contribute to deepening bilateral cooperation in relevant fields and enhancing friendship between the two peoples. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: Xi meets president of Swiss Confederation, calling for more certainty for China-Europe economic, trade cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30
Xi meets president of Swiss Confederation, calling for more certainty for China-Europe economic, trade cooperation Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with President of the Swiss Confederation Guy Parmelin, who is paying a working visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) BEIJING, Oct. 30 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping met with President of the Swiss Confederation Guy Parmelin in Beijing on Friday, calling on both countries to inject confidence and more certainty into China-Europe economic and trade cooperation as well as into the global economic development. Noting Switzerland is an important partner of China in Europe, Xi said Swiss cooperation with China has always been at the forefront among European countries. He added that free trade cooperation has become the brightest highlight of China-Switzerland relations, which fully demonstrates the political courage and responsibility of the two countries in adhering to open cooperation, and highlights the unique leading role of both sides in promoting the building of an open world economy. China is willing to work with Switzerland to uphold openness, strengthen cooperation, promote a universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization, and jointly inject confidence and more certainty into the economic and trade cooperation between China and European countries, as well as into the global economic development, Xi said. Since the establishment of diplomatic ties, China and Switzerland have continuously translated the China-Switzerland cooperation spirit, featuring equality, innovation and win-win results, into pragmatic outcomes, setting a model for interactions between countries of different sizes and with different social systems, Xi pointed out. He said the two sides should respect each other, treat each other as equals, and comprehensively enhance exchanges and policy alignment at different levels. Noting that China is accelerating the development of new quality productive forces and steadily expanding institutional opening up, Xi said the country is ready to turn its market into a market for the world and a shared market for all. Both sides should adhere to mutual benefit and win-win results, strengthen innovation cooperation and focus on fostering cooperation in emerging industries, including digital economy, green energy storage and artificial intelligence, he added. Xi expressed hope that Switzerland would leverage its unique influence to actively promote balanced and stable development of trade between China and European countries. As China and Switzerland share similar positions and concepts in supporting multilateralism, Xi said both sides should deepen multilateral coordination and mutual support, firmly uphold the international system with the United Nations at its core and the international order based on international law, reform and improve the global governance system, and advance the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. Parmelin said that since the establishment of diplomatic relations, Switzerland and China have always respected each other, maintained close high-level exchanges, and achieved fruitful cooperation results in many fields such as trade and investment, scientific research and innovation, and employment. Noting that this year marks the 10th anniversary of the establishment of Switzerland-China innovative strategic partnership, Parmelin said that the two sides have successfully completed negotiations on signing a protocol on upgrading free trade agreement in a short period of time with high quality, demonstrating a high level of mutual trust between the two sides, which will inject new impetus into bilateral relations. Switzerland firmly adheres to the one-China policy and looks forward to strengthening dialogue and exchanges with China, upholding mutually beneficial cooperation, and promoting greater development in cooperation in various fields, he said. The Swiss side attaches great importance to the positive role played by China in international affairs and is willing to closely coordinate with China, adhere to multilateralism, safeguard free trade, and contribute to world development, prosperity, peace and stability, Parmelin added. After their meeting, the two leaders witnessed the signing of the protocol on upgrading free trade agreement and multiple cooperation documents in areas like scientific research, employment and the media. item.title: Xi holds talks with German president, calls for opening new chapter in all-round strategic partnership
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30
Xi holds talks with German president, calls for opening new chapter in all-round strategic partnership Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan pose for a group photo with German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier and his wife Elke Budenbender prior to the talks between Xi and Steinmeier at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 30, 2026. Xi held talks with Steinmeier, who is on a state visit to China, in Beijing on Friday. (Xinhua/Shen Hong) BEIJING, Oct. 30 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping held talks with German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier in Beijing on Friday, saying China is ready to work with Germany to open a new chapter in China-Germany all-round strategic partnership and promote the building of a more just and equitable global governance system. Xi said as the world's second and third largest economies, China and Germany bear significant responsibilities for the development of China-EU relations and the stable growth of the world economy. Xi called on both sides to enhance communication and collaboration, create a new model of cooperation featuring equality, mutual benefit and strategic stability, and send out positive signals to the world of choosing openness over isolation and cooperation over confrontation. China's policy toward Germany is consistent, stable and predictable, and China is happy to see Germany play a greater role in European and international affairs, Xi said, noting that China has attached great importance to Germany's status as a major country and always supported its reunification and development. Xi expressed hope that Germany will view China's development and its cooperation with China with an open and positive attitude, uphold a rational, pragmatic and friendly policy toward China, and adhere to mutual respect and equal treatment, which is a valuable piece of experience for the sustained and sound development of China-Germany relations. Noting that Germany is a representative of advanced manufacturing and high-quality products, while China is advancing its modernization through high-quality development, Xi said the two sides have compatible development strategies and broad space for cooperation. Xi said China welcomes enterprises from Germany and other countries to deepen their presence in China and share the benefit of its supersized market. It is hoped that the German side will provide a fair, transparent and non-discriminatory business environment for Chinese enterprises operating in Germany, he added. Xi expressed China's willingness to cooperate with Germany in areas such as artificial intelligence, green and low-carbon development, trade in services and digital economy to jointly enhance future competitiveness. Both sides should support cultural, educational and artistic exchanges, facilitate personnel exchanges, foster people-to-people connectivity, and create a favorable atmosphere for celebrating the 55th anniversary of bilateral ties next year, Xi said. China has always viewed the EU as a partner, and is committed to developing China-EU relations with sincerity and goodwill, said Xi, adding that history and reality have repeatedly shown that for China and the EU, cooperation outweighs competition and consensus outweighs differences. He added that as long as both China and the EU stay committed to the positioning of their partnership and maintain the tone of equal-footed dialogue, differences and problems can be resolved and will not hinder further development of China-EU relations. It is hoped that the EU will work with China in the same direction to jointly advance an equal and orderly multipolar world and a universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization, Xi said. Xi briefed Steinmeier on the fifth plenary session of the 20th Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, adding that the CPC is willing to exchange governance experience with major political parties around the world, including those in Germany. Steinmeier, who is on a state visit to China, said that over the past 25 years, he has visited China eight times. Hailing China's rapid development, Steinmeier said China has become a major country with considerable political influence as well as economic, scientific and technological strength. Germany greatly admires the tremendous development achievements China has made under the leadership of President Xi, he noted. Germany firmly adheres to the one-China policy and is fully confident about the prospects of bilateral relations, Steinmeier said. The two countries can properly resolve economic and trade differences via dialogue and consultation to achieve win-win results, setting an example for the world, he said. Noting that the international order is under strain, and the world expects China to play a bigger role, Steinmeier said Germany is ready to jointly shoulder the responsibility of safeguarding world peace and development with China, uphold the purposes and principles of the UN Charter and the authority of international law, support free trade and WTO rules, and oppose protectionism and trade wars. Prior to the talks, Xi and his wife Peng Liyuan held a welcoming ceremony for Steinmeier and his wife Elke Büdenbender at the square outside the east entrance of the Great Hall of the People. Xi and Peng also held a welcoming banquet for Steinmeier and Büdenbender on Friday evening. item.description:

Home>>
Xi stresses Party self-governance to ensure CPC remains strong leadership core (Xinhua) 15:59, October 30, 2026 BEIJING, Oct. 30 (Xinhua) -- Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, stressed the need to persevere with full and rigorous Party self-governance to ensure that the CPC remains the strong leadership core in advancing socialism with Chinese characteristics. Xi made the remarks at a symposium on Aug. 21 to solicit opinions from non-Party personages on drafting the resolution of the CPC Central Committee on certain major issues concerning persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance. The resolution was adopted at the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the CPC, which concluded on Thursday in Beijing.
